newsitem.title: USA: ShopKo says Supervalu shrs to sell at $25.
newsitem.headline: ShopKo says Supervalu shrs to sell at $25.

text.p: ShopKo Stores Inc said a secondary offering of 6.56 million common shares being sold by Supervalu Inc was priced at $25 per share.
The closing of the offering and ShopKo's repurchase of an additional 8.17 million common shares from Supervalu is scheduled to occur on July 2, ShopKo said.
ShopKo said it granted underwriters an option to purchase up to 983,592 additional shares to cover over-allotments.
The secondary offering and the buyback are part of a deal in which Supervalu will sell its 46-percent investment in ShopKo, which Supervalu has held since 1971.
In a separate announcement, Minneapolis-based Supervalu said it expects to receive net proceeds from the secondary offering of about $155 million, after underwriting expenses.
It also reiterated that the price for the sale of its 8.2-million share ShopKo position back to ShopKo was $18.35 per share, or about $150 million.
Supervalu said it plans to use proceeds from these transactions to repurchase its shares. To date, the company has bought back about 900,000 shares, it said.

ShopKo operates 130 retail stores and four free-standing optical centers in 16 states, concentrated in the Upper Midwest, Western Mountain and Pacific Northwest states. It also has a ProVantage Inc unit that specializes in prescription benefit management, vision benefit management and health information technology.

Supervalu is a major food distributor and food retailer. It serves about 4,400 food stores in 48 states and 638 limited assortment stores through its Save-A-Lot operations. It also operates 319 food retail stores.
